clue.text: Costume apt to succeed abroad

indicators.note: to succeed is to come after, so the word for apt follows the word for abroad

parts.note: out means away from home, as abroad does
apt and fit both mean suitable

explanation.surface: Advice that a costume is a good choice for a trip overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is a set of clothes worn together, the same thing as a costume.

clue.text: Theatrical performance requiring exercise in voice production

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech, a production of the voice
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A stage show demands training in how to project the voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatrical' points to the operating theatre: surgery is performed there.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery is carried out in an operating theatre, so a surgical procedure is a performance in a theatre.

clue.text: Pitch covered about one,'so lost time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for pitch covered goes round one

parts.note: tarred means coated with pitch
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricket pitch was covered, so a player was delayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is to delay or linger, so having tarried means having lost time.

clue.text: A brave group taken up by swingers

parts.note: a brave is an old term for a Native American warrior, called an Indian in older usage
a club is a group or society

explanation.surface: A courageous society is adopted by fun-seekers.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian clubs are bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in pairs for exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: These exercise weights are picked up and swung round, so swingers take them up.

clue.text: Wise to swallow medicine for upset

indicators.note: to swallow is to take something inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: sage means wise
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: It would be sensible to take a tablet for an upset stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillage is a knocking over of liquid, an upset in the sense of a spill.

clue.text: Making progress by a foot or two

definitions.text: Making progress by a foot or two

parts.words: Making progress by a foot or two
parts.note: suggests inching forward a short distance, but means moving along by pushing with the feet, as on a bicycle

explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist moves forward by pushing on the cranks with one foot and then the other.

clue.text: Fired when key inserted, it gives a boost

indicators.note: inserted means put inside, so the key letter goes into the word for fired

parts.note: lit means set on fire
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Once the ignition key is turned the engine fires and gives a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift raises something up, or cheers someone, giving them a boost.

clue.text: Battle account including name and dates recorded here

indicators.note: including means holding inside, so the battle and account go round the name

parts.note: the Alma was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War

explanation.surface: A history of a battle including names and dates is written down.
explanation.walkthrough: ALMA is the river in Crimea where an 1854 battle was fought.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a yearly calendar listing dates, events and tables.

clue.text: Give notice in 13

annotationWithheld.why: Give notice in 13: printed so on the scan; the answer is 13-across ENOW with D added, but no clue word gives D ('notice' is not D; 'note' would be)

clue.text: Pirate's ungrammatical self-identification

parts.note: a pirate announcing himself with the casual 'It's me' instead of the correct 'It is I', with the first word clipped

explanation.definitionFit: Smee is Captain Hook's bosun in Peter Pan, and the name sounds like ''s me', a careless way of saying who you are.

clue.text: Party member initially has real trouble before ennoblement

indicators.note: before puts the rearranged letters ahead of the party and initial
trouble suggests the letters of real are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of member

explanation.surface: A political party member has real problems before being given a peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' turns REAL into EARL, which comes 'before' DO plus the first letter of 'member'.
explanation.definitionFit: An earldom is the rank of an earl, so being made one is an ennoblement.

clue.text: Ran down English celebrity in outskirts of Dortmund

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Dortmund

parts.note: celebrity and fame both mean renown

explanation.surface: A famous English person was disparaged on the edge of a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives DD, the first and last letters of Dortmund, and 'in' puts E plus FAME between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise or slander them, which is what defaming means.

clue.text: Lady in team dances in lively style

indicators.note: dances suggests the letters of lady, in and team move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman in a troupe dances with great energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' rearranges LADY, IN and TEAM, ten letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with animation means doing it with liveliness and spirit.

clue.text: Old enough to find diversion in new love?

indicators.note: a diversion turns things aside from their course, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are mature enough to find a distraction in a new romance.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for sufficient, an old form of enough found in older poetry.

clue.text: A complete change for Grimes, say, on his' day off

definitions.text: Grimes, say, on his' day off

explanation.walkthrough: Mr Grimes is the chimney sweep in Charles Kingsley's novel The Water-Babies; off work, he would be clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A total transformation is a complete clear-out; and a chimney cleaner who has washed for once is a spotless one.

clue.text: Exponents of mathematics

parts.note: reads as people who champion mathematics, but exponents are also the small raised powers in algebra

explanation.definitionFit: In algebra the small raised powers such as squares and cubes are also called exponents.

clue.text: She appears' in article that is written after stage hit's opening

indicators.note: written after places the article and that-is pieces behind the stage and opening

parts.note: a step is a stage in a process

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of hit

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A woman features in a newspaper piece about a stage play's first night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the whole definition: the answer is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephanie is a girl's name, so it can stand for a she.

clue.text: Disorder here in French square is against the law

parts.note: an ill is a disorder or ailment
ici is French for here
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: A rowdy disturbance in a French town square is forbidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, unlawful.

clue.text: Nursery entrant has Derby date switched

indicators.note: switched means changed around, so the letters of Derby and date swap places

explanation.surface: A horse entered for the Derby has had its race day changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrant' and 'Derby' suggest a horse race, but the entrant is a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuddly toy found in a child's room is a newcomer to the nursery.

clue.text: Writer turns to music — of the spheres?

indicators.note: turns tells us the word for writer is read from right to left

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: An author takes up composing, perhaps the celestial music of the spheres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' makes NEP from PEN. The 'music of the spheres' was the old idea of harmony made by the planets; the question mark says the definition names one of those spheres, a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is a planet, one of the heavenly bodies the ancients called spheres.

clue.text: Controversy about to, hold up European motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, to hold up something is to sit beneath it

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland, a European
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: An argument about holding up traffic on a European motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London to Leeds motorway; read as letters it is MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A polemic is a strongly argued attack, a piece of controversy.

clue.text: Ambitious Indian territory chief

parts.note: Goa is a state on the west coast of India, formerly Portuguese
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: A leader of a region of India is described as driven.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person is enterprising and keen to get on.

clue.text: Veil with fasteners in: centre of sleeve

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
the centre of the six-letter word sleeve is its middle two letters

parts.note: clips are fasteners

explanation.surface: A dress-making note about a veil attached with clips to the middle of a sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' gives EE from sleeve, and 'in' puts CLIPS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to obscure or hide from view, as a veil does.

clue.text: Part in carol easily learned

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words carol easily

explanation.surface: A singer's part in a Christmas carol is quickly memorised.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'caROL Easily'; 'learned' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part an actor or singer takes in a performance.

clue.text: Sports car drivers overcoming hesitation?.

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcoming means sitting on top of, so the drivers come first

parts.note: the RAC, the Royal Automobile Club, is a British motorists' organisation
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Sports car drivers getting past their nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring body.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is a car built for racing or speed.

clue.text: Peter Pan possibly not finding it difficult

explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is a play for children, and something no harder than a children's game is very easy.

clue.text: Endure to the end

explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on enduring; and the last is the end, as in 'faithful to the last'.

clue.text: Operatic heroine repeating note

indicators.note: repeating means the note appears twice in a row

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An opera heroine sings the same note over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme.

clue.text: Bloomer made by defender without aspiration

indicators.note: without tells us a letter is taken out of the word for defender

parts.note: a champion defends a cause or a title
aspiration is the breathy h sound, so it stands for the letter H

explanation.surface: A mistake made by a defender who has lost his ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder to go with the defender, but it is a flower. 'without' drops H, the aspirate, from CHAMPION.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a wild flower, and a flower is a bloomer in crossword language.

clue.text: Record incorporated in stone tablet in part of church

indicators.note: incorporated in means taken into the body of something, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a stele is an upright inscribed stone slab
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record of events is carved on a stone tablet inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A STELE is an inscribed stone slab from the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is the tall tower and spire on a church.

clue.text: One taking delivery of a hearing aid, perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: A recipient takes delivery of goods, and the earpiece of a telephone or a radio set helps one hear.

clue.text: A paper in trouble, that's manifest

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters of paper are in disarray and rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper is clearly in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges PAPER into PPEAR after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest is to show up or become visible, a verb sense.
